subject: Day 26: high-contrast card session
bodyText:
Today's focus
At 26 days Avi prefers human faces and bold contrast over everything else, and he is starting to recognize your voices. Today leans into visual fixation and the back-and-forth that builds language.

Action items
- Run a short high-contrast card session today, holding bold black-and-white cards 8-12 inches from his face and letting him lock on and track. AAP baby senses: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- Confirm the 400 IU/day vitamin D supplement is in his daily routine; AAP advises it for breastfed and predominantly breastfed infants regardless of how much daylight he gets. AAP vitamin D: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-D-On-the-Double.aspx
- If you are returning to work at 12 or 16 weeks, start daycare and nanny research in earnest this week; top Bay Area daycares run 6-18 month waitlists and nanny searches take 4-8 weeks.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Wet sneezing, hiccups after feeds, and a quiet startle at loud sounds are all normal reflex activity at this stage.
- [monitor] Frequent painful spit-up with arching during or after feeds, or feed refusal despite clear hunger cues, may point to GERD or cow's-milk-protein intolerance; note it for the 1-month visit.
- [call within 24h] A persistent inability to console combined with back-arching during feeds should be raised same-day to sort severe reflux from milk-protein intolerance.
- [call now] A rectal temperature of 100.4F or higher, cyanosis around the lips, or seizure-like movement means call the pediatrician or 911 right now!

Enrichment opportunities
- Hold high-contrast black-and-white cards 8-12 inches out and move them slowly side to side; at this age he prefers faces and bold contrast, so let him fixate before you shift. AAP baby senses: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- Answer every coo as if he spoke a full sentence, pause, then answer his next sound; this serve-and-return turn-taking is the pattern Romeo et al. linked to stronger later language. Romeo et al. 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/
- Take a 20-30 minute daylight stroller walk for varied sensory input and your own cardiovascular recovery; the outdoor light and motion are good input even though the vitamin D supplement does the nutritional work. AAP vitamin D: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-D-On-the-Double.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit; bring the feeding and output log
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit; vaccines HepB #2, RV #1, DTaP #1, Hib #1, PCV #1, IPV #1
- Day 57-72: post-2-month-vaccine window; expect 24-48h of fussiness and low-grade fever

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete

- Follows a moving object with eyes past midline
  AAP window: day 28-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Hold a small object 8-12 inches away and slowly move side to side. Eyes should cross the body midline.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-moving-object/complete

- Seems happy to see you when you walk up
  AAP window: day 28-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Recognition + positive affect. Often accompanied by limb-pumping excitement.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/seems-happy-to-see-you/complete

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60 (coming up)
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete
